Redisa 2016

By: Joy Summers | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Redisa's empire is crumbling - we bring you explosive new evidence

Summary:
REDISA 2016 A damning letter

Since 2012 Carte Blanche has been questioning the Redisa tyre plan. In 2015 we exposed the failures of the plan. Contrary to its job creation targets these had not been met, we questioned the conflict of interest between Redisa a not for profit company and its management company Kusaga Taga. We questioned the R600 million rand flowing into its coffers every year and Redisa’s failure to create a viable tyre manufacturing industry. At the time the department refused to speak on the record to Carte Blanche and the minister of the environment was publicly singing Redisa’s praises.

Well one year later, Redisa finds itself firmly on the backfoot. Treasury has insisted that the tyre tax will no longer be going to Redisa, but to Treasury itself from February 2017.

Hermann Erdmann has naturally been fighting all the way and even taken on the minister herself to prevent the DEA from cutting off his funding.



Further information:
Now in an explosive set of documents Carte Blanche can reveal that Redisa’s days are indeed numbered. On the 31st of October the minister signed a letter and sent it to HERMANN ERDMANN giving him 15 working days to explain why she should not withdraw the REDISA PLAN. The letter sets out many of the concerns first flagged by Carte Blanche- failure to create jobs, fraudulently adding job opportunities rather than jobs, a conflict of interest between KT and Redisa, failure to create a viable recycling industry, and possible criminal charges levelled at the Midrand depot.

Armed with a new forensic report commissioned by the department and a payment schedule that shows the millions raked in by KT, money misspent by Redisa on luxury office furniture, the Snip and Cut hair salon that runs into thousands of rands, scan for life body scans, luxury picnics, millions on PR and investments that are questionable, we go back to this story as Mr Hermann Erdmann’s empire begins to collapse.

Script:


Redisa final script 2016

Commentary one
In 2012 the Department of environment gazetted a waste tyre management plan. It’s called Redisa and its primary objective was to use waste tyres to generate 10 000 jobs in five years and create a recycling industry. Hermann Erdmann, its CEO, is Redisa’s champion

Hermann Erdmann interview 2014
This is more and bigger than me and individuals, this is about the future of my children and developing a viable recycling industry throughout South Africa

Commentary Two
Redisa’s plan involves micro collectors who pick up the tyres, take them to smaller and larger depots, where they are collected by transporters who are supposed to take them to recyclers to make rubber crumb, oil and other products. For that, Redisa gets paid around R600 million a year by the big manufacturers who add it to the price of your tyres, as a tax.

Link
What if you found out that one of the taxes you pay had bypassed Treasury and ended up in the pockets of a handful of wealthy individuals who seem to like the finer things in life?

Commentary Three
That’s what Redisa looked like to Jan Jooste, director of innovation at the Vaal University of Technology. He wrote a report on the plan in 2012. It was vague, he said. All Redisa had to do was collect nine tyres and get paid R600 million rand. Four years later he hasn’t changed his mind.

Devi
So far you haven’t ticked any of the boxes?
Jan
I don’t think we are going to tick any, unless we get to personal enrichment

Commentary Four
Hermann Erdmann, Charlie Kirk and Stacey Davidson are Redisa’s executive directors. Every time you buy a new tyre, you pay R2 30 per kilogramme to Redisa

Devi
The tax is deducted before you even buy the tyres so people think what is the big deal?
Jan Jooste
The big deal is that R2 billion rand of SA money has been channeled to individuals, whereas that R2 billion rand could have been channeled to create a whole new industry in order to create hope for thousands of people.

Commentary Five
Last year Carte Blanche exposed how Erdmann travelled the world, and lived a life of luxury while Redisa paid a miserly R2 per tyre to their micro collectors, fed the Department with fraudulent job figures, and instead of creating a recycling industry was exporting large quantities of tyres, in violation of the gazetted plan. But Redisa had convinced the minister otherwise

Minister Edna Molewa
The fact that so many countries of the world are saying this is an envy, and we are actually path finders, an example that has got to lead the world.

Commentary Six
This year, Redisa’s payment schedules over 22 months were leaked to Carte Blanche.

Devi
Shamwari game reserve R194 000!
Jan
Exactly
Devi
Dial a picnic: R12 900?

Commentary Seven
The payments paint an astonishing picture of excess.

Devi
Sleep world R25 000 did the tyres need a rest?
Jan Jooste
If the AG were to look at this all of this, his hair would fall out

Commentary eight
But Redisa frown upon any story that contradicts their narrative, one carefully developed by spending well over R19 million on PR and marketing

Hermann Erdmann
It’s for us very heartwarming to be recognized, and to be able to do something which can potentially change the world

Commentary nine
Cross them and they spend millions more on attorneys.

Up sound Jan
One legal firm earned R5.6 million rand

Commentary ten
After our expose the Department initiated an investigation and Redisa in turn, filed legal papers against Carte Blanche.

LINK
This year something shifted. This letter leaked to Carte Blanche, signed by minister Edna Molewa to Hermann Erdmann, and it’s a damning indictment of the Redisa plan.

Commentary eleven
Signed at the end of last month, the minister has given Hermann Erdmann 15 working days to convince her, with documents, why she should not consider the withdrawal of the Redisa plan

Jan
What is heartening now, is that government is now questioning Erdmann’s execution of the plan

Commentary twelve
She notes that the plan was approved on condition that Redisa would properly account and report to the DEA

LINK
So one would think that when the minister requests documents, Hermann Erdmann and his directors would jump. They didn’t, even the minister had trouble prizing documents from Redisa

Commentary Thirteen
Redisa share a floor of these offices with a for profit management company called Kusaga Taka consulting. But in this performance report, commissioned by the department, it cautions that three of Redisa’s directors are shareholders of Kusaga Taka consulting, which it says does not auger well for the principles of good governance

Devi
Kusaga Taga takes 18%. What does that work out to?
Jan
R108 million per year.
Devi
Big money?
Jan
Ya that is serious money!

Commentary fourteen
In 2014 Herman Edmann brushed off our concerns
Devi
What is your shareholding in Kusaga Taga
Hermann
I own part of the company
Devi
So that is the point, there is this conflict of interest, you have one foot in Redisa and the other firmly planted in Kusaga Taga?
Hermann
Well, first of all, conflict of interest exists in industry many times
Devi
It mustn’t.
Hermann
No, that is not true, I think they must not influence you negatively. The mere fact is I make this thing, is not the problem, the fact is, will I perform is the problem?

LINK
We have always questioned the conflict of interest between Redisa and KusagaTaka, but now even the minister is concerned, and she can’t get any answers! In her letter she says when called upon to account for such funds Redisa proceeds to hide behind the confidentiality of the private entity, namely Kusaga Taka that received the management fee

Commentary fifteen
And the performance audit, has found so far, that the management costs versus the programme costs appear to be exorbitant

Up sound Jan
Now the payment schedule we have unfortunately only covers 22 months, but over the 22 months we should have seen a transfer in the region of R200 million rand going to Kusaga Taga, it seems there is R389 million that goes to Kusaga Taga, so almost R190 million more than should have gone there

Devi
Spilhaus, nice crystal. There were payments for Koi fish, ice cream, haircuts!
You see I am trying to understand where is the recycling value in ice cream, crystal and haircuts.
Jan
Ya it seems they received R24 000, maybe they are cutting tyres, hopefully

LINK
In the meantime, Hermann Erdmann, and some of his co- directors have created a nest egg for themselves in the Eastern Cape using Redisa money. The minister suspects that is yet another channel for the enrichment of certain individuals

Commentary sixteen
Hermann Erdmann, Kusaga Taga’s Chris Crozier and Xolani Qubeka, chairperson of Redisa’s board are all directors of the Product Testing institute. They plan to test new tyres coming into South Africa.

Jan Jooste
It seems from the minister’s letter that no such permission was gathered from the department, plus this testing facility is outside the plan, so in fact then it is illegal

Commentary seventeen
Dr. Ziboneni Godongwana has a PHD in chemistry. He was former head of Research and development at Kusgaka Taka, and was brought into the meetings about the testing facility




Ziboneni Godongwana
It really shocked me that this is a private company belonging to an individual and money was taken from the recycling of tyres, into the testing of tyres which I don’t think was the mandate of the DEA to Redisa

Commentary seventeen
Previously he had blown the whistle on fraud in the company and Ziboneni believes the directors were nervous he would blow the whistle on the Product Testing Institute. Eventually he says he was squeezed out

Ziboneni
It was like hell on earth, you do your best but someone is trying to find fault with whatever you do

Commentary eighteen
For the last ten months he has been unable to find employment. Meanwhile building has begun at the institute. The minister says R60 million rand has been diverted. Ziboneni says it’s a lot more

Ziboneni
Everything that happened was embedded in corruption. If they saw that you were honest, then they would find a way to get rid of you

Commentary nineteen
Now, the department is tightening the screws on Redisa. In her letter the minister says Redisa has failed to create even a quarter of the 10 000 jobs. The Department confirmed to Carte Blanche Redisa’s job creation targets are under investigation

Jan Jooste
I think its part of Redisa’s game to have this smoke and mirrors as to exactly how many jobs are created

Commentary twenty
The performance report and the ministers letter make it abundantly clear that Redisa has failed to create a recycling industry. Apart from that she calls Redisa to account in terms of governance, deviations from the plan, a loan made they shouldn’t have, refusal to provide complete records, and their development of SMME’S. Lastly the fact that Redisa is now taking the department to court, at tax payers expense.

Jan Jooste
Redisa is in effect using taxpayer money to fight the taxpayer in court, as represented by government, and the irony is that the taxpayer is now funding Redisa, fighting for the opportunity, to in fact steal more.

THE END 10 mins 21 seconds


PROMO ONE 10 seconds
Redisa’s waste tyre management plan was supposed to create 10 000 jobs and set up a recycling industry. Now, Minister Edna Molewa has called Redisa to account

PROMO TWO 15 seconds
How has Redisa been spending your tyre tax?

Devi
Shamwari game reserve R194 000!
Jan
Exactly
Devi
Sleep world R25 000 did the tyres need a rest?
Jan Jooste
If the AG were to look at this all of this, his hair would fall out


PROMO THREE

Hermann Erdmann interview 2014
This is about the future of my children and developing a viable recycling industry throughout South Africa

Commentary
Has Redisa’s Hermann Erdmann fulfilled his promise to create a tyre recycling industry
